topics.title: Identify the environment
topics.summary: cat /etc/os-release identifies the distribution. uname -r identifies the running kernel. systemctl --version identifies the installed systemd tools; it does not by itself prove that this environment boots with systemd. ps -p 1 -o pid,comm,args identifies the visible PID 1. Read Chapters 1, 7, and 8 when those answers seem inconsistent.

topics.title: Find a path or permission boundary
topics.summary: pwd -P shows the current physical directory. ls -ld PATH inspects the directory entry rather than listing its contents. namei -l PATH traces pathname components where installed. id, getfacl PATH, ls -Z PATH, and the service’s effective configuration reveal different access layers. A user-shell write test is not automatically equivalent to a sandboxed service write. See Chapters 3–5 and 18.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix A — Find the next useful command
topics.title: Understand storage pressure
topics.summary: df -hT reports filesystem block capacity and type. df -i reports inode capacity. du -x -h DIRECTORY accounts for reachable directory entries on one filesystem. findmnt --target PATH identifies the containing mount. lsof +L1 can identify open unlinked files, subject to access and scope. None of these commands alone identifies every cause of a full filesystem. See Chapters 9, 21, 23, and 32.

topics.title: Understand a process
topics.summary: ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm shows a selected process view. top samples changing activity. pidstat -u -r -d 1 5 collects bounded process measurements when sysstat is installed. A PID is a current identifier, not a permanent application identity. Check the process start time and owner before signaling a reused number. See Chapters 7 and 22.

topics.title: Understand a systemd service
topics.summary: systemctl status NAME.service --no-pager provides a useful summary. systemctl cat NAME.service shows unit files and drop-ins. systemctl show NAME.service exposes manager properties. journalctl -u NAME.service --since '-10 minutes' retrieves a time-scoped log view. A unit can be active while its application is unhealthy, and an enabled unit can currently be stopped. See Chapters 8, 14, and 23.

topics.summary: ip -br address, ip route, and ip route get DESTINATION answer address and route questions. ss -lntp inspects TCP listeners. getent hosts NAME follows the configured system name-service path; dig NAME asks DNS. curl tests an application request and can validate HTTPS when name and trust are correct. topics.title: Validate a candidate before applying it
topics.summary: bash -n SCRIPT checks Bash syntax, not behavior. sshd -t validates SSH server configuration, not every user’s ability to log in. nginx -t validates the complete NGINX configuration and some referenced resources, not the entire client path. findmnt --verify --tab-file FILE inspects an fstab candidate, not every future storage condition. A validation command is one gate, followed by application-level verification and recovery planning.

topics.title: Read an error as evidence
topics.summary: Record the exact command, host, identity, timestamp, exit status, and relevant output. Separate a refused connection from a timeout, an absent DNS name from a resolver that cannot answer, a permission denial from a nonexistent path, and a full filesystem from a full directory assumption. These distinctions reduce both wasted effort and dangerous changes.
